meta.phaseName: Capital structure, balance-sheet risk & returns on capital
assumedContext: Network egress blocked except the search index; the year-by-year maturity ladder, the FY2026 D&A figure and the 2016-2020 invested-capital series could not be retrieved.

The ~$279bn of not-yet-commenced leases is NOT added to net debt, because Phase 5's free-cash-flow forecast already carries lease payments through operating cash flow and finance-lease principal inside capex. Adding it to net debt would double-count.
Invested capital of $254.8bn is derived from BVPS $102.52 x 2.55bn shares plus $83.66bn debt less $90.26bn cash and securities.

findings.claim: Invested capital at 2026-06-30 is approximately $254.8bn: equity ~$261.4bn (BVPS $102.52 x 2.55bn shares) plus $83.66bn long-term debt less $90.26bn cash and marketable securities. Reported net debt is negative $6.6bn - a net cash position.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Derived from Meta Q2 2026 10-Q balance-sheet items (long-term debt $83.66bn, cash and securities $90.26bn) and reported Q2 2026 book value per share of $102.52

findings.claim: Meta issued $30bn of senior unsecured notes on 2025-10-30 (30-year at +98bp, 40-year at +110bp, on a $125bn order book) and $25bn in May 2026 in six series maturing 2031-2066 with coupons of 4.55%-6.45%. Long-term debt stood at $83.66bn at 2026-06-30 with no near-term maturity wall.
findings.label: FACT
findings.source: Meta Q2 2026 10-Q; market reporting on the October 2025 and May 2026 issues

findings.claim: Interest expense rose $542m (+225%) in Q2 2026 and $864m (+180%) in H1 2026 versus the prior-year periods, off FY2025 interest expense of $1,165m, implying a FY2026 run-rate near $3.1bn and $6-8bn by 2028 at a $50bn annual issuance pace.
findings.label: FACT
findings.unit: USD m implied FY2026 interest expense
findings.source: Meta Q2 2026 10-Q interest-expense disclosure; FY2025 interest expense per FY2025 results

findings.claim: S&P affirmed AA- with a stable outlook (2025-02-05) and Moody's affirmed Aa3 stable, projecting total debt/EBITDA below 1.0x for YE2026 and YE2027 and revenue growth above 20% in 2026 and 18% in 2027. In July 2026 Moody's warned that unprecedented AI spending threatens the credit quality of Amazon, Meta and Alphabet.
findings.label: FACT
findings.source: cbonds report of S&P affirmation 2025-02-05; Investing.com report of Moody's affirmation; CNBC 2026-07-24 on the Moody's sector warning

findings.claim: Debt headroom against the rating agencies' modelled 1.0x total debt/EBITDA is roughly $36bn on FY2026E EBITDA of ~$120bn - about three months of capex at the guided run-rate. At 2.0x the headroom is ~$156bn, about thirteen months. No statutory issuance cap or binding covenant was identified.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Derived from Moody's stated sub-1.0x expectation and an estimated FY2026E EBITDA of ~$120bn (operating income ~$85bn plus ~$35bn D&A)

findings.claim: Estimated funding gap of about $6.9bn in FY2026 and $5.5bn in FY2027 (operating cash flow less capex, dividends and maturities), covered by the $25bn May 2026 issuance. The gap assumes zero buybacks: shareholders are the residual funder of the capital programme through the return they are not receiving.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Derived from Phase 3 cash-flow work and FY2026 capex guidance of $130-145bn

findings.claim: Historical ROIC (GuruFocus, constant definition): 43.26% (2021), 20.47% (2022), 27.09% (2023), 34.25% (2024), 36.85% (2025), 32.39% (Q1 2026 annualised), against an estimated WACC of 7.3-9.5% - a positive spread of 12 to 36 points in every year for which data exists.
findings.label: FACT
findings.source: GuruFocus META ROIC page, retrieved 2026-09-06; WACC series is an analyst estimate on a constant method (risk-free plus 1.15 x 4.5% ERP)

findings.claim: Incremental ROIC on the current capital vintage is 1.4% for 2025-2026E (delta NOPAT $1.4bn on delta invested capital ~$103bn) and 6.4% for 2025-2028E (delta NOPAT $22.4bn on ~$350bn), both below a 9.5% WACC. Meta is consuming the excess returns of its legacy franchise to fund a programme earning below its cost of capital.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Derived at a 16% tax rate from FY2025 actual operating income, FY2026 expense guidance, an FY2028E operating income estimate of $110bn, and capex less estimated D&A

findings.claim: The 2025-28 capital vintage clears a 9.5% cost of capital at an FY2028 operating income of $122.9bn - a 35.3% operating margin on ~$348bn of revenue, versus 41.4% in FY2025 and an estimated 33.7% in FY2026. The repair is arithmetically specific and within management's control.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Derived: required delta NOPAT of $33.3bn (=$350bn x 9.5%) grossed up at a 16% tax rate and added to FY2025 operating income of $83.28bn

findings.claim: The dominant sensitivity is the discount rate, not the income statement: a 100bp rise in WACC cuts base-case DCF value by roughly 17% (about $85 per share) while costing the credit only about $1bn a year of pre-tax income. The US 10-year Treasury at 4.79% on 2026-09-04, its highest since November 2023, is a large part of why the shares fell 15% over twelve months while revenue grew 28%.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Treasury yield per CNBC/TradingEconomics 2026-09-04; DCF sensitivity derived from the Phase 5 base-case model

findings.claim: About 56% of revenue is non-US (Q2 2026: Europe $14.3bn, Asia-Pacific $11.2bn, Rest of World $8.5bn of $60.3bn regional revenue) against an overwhelmingly USD cost base, so a 10% move in the dollar moves operating income by about $14.1bn, roughly 17%, with no offset.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.unit: USD m operating income effect per 10% USD move
findings.source: Derived from Meta Q2 2026 regional revenue disclosure, assuming full translation pass-through and no local-currency price response

findings.claim: The sector-relevant input-cost shock is the useful life of a GPU. Cutting server life from 5.5 to 4.0 years would add roughly $20bn to FY2028 depreciation (about 18% of operating income); extending it to 7.0 years would cut D&A by roughly $12bn with zero cash effect. The FY2022 precedent shows the operating leverage: revenue fell 1% and operating income fell 38%, from $46.75bn to $28.94bn.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.unit: USD m FY2028 D&A increase if life cut to 4.0 years
findings.source: Derived from the cumulative 2025-28 IT capital base and Meta's 5.5-year policy disclosed 2025-01-29; FY2022 figures per Meta historical income statements

risks.text: Incremental ROIC of 1-6% against a 9.5% WACC: the franchise's excess returns are funding a programme that earns below its cost of capital
Rating headroom of roughly $36bn against the agencies' modelled sub-1.0x debt/EBITDA is about three months of capex; a downgrade path would raise the cost of the next $100bn
A 100bp rise in the discount rate removes ~17% of equity value because ~87% of DCF value sits in the terminal value - the risk that has already driven the 15% twelve-month de-rating
A 10% stronger dollar costs roughly $14.1bn of operating income, about 17%, with no cost-side offset
Shortening server life to 4 years would add ~$20bn to FY2028 depreciation, ~18% of operating income, with no change in cash

catalysts.text: FY2027 capex guidance - the disclosure that resolves the central variable
First quarter of positive incremental operating margin above 20%, evidencing the plateau
Rating action or outlook change from Moody's or S&P on AI capital intensity
Resumption of buybacks against the $25.03bn unused authorisation
Equity issuance to fund the programme - the single most negative capital-allocation signal available

conclusions: The balance sheet funds the plan comfortably for now: AA-/Aa3, no near-term maturity wall, a ~$6.9bn FY2026 funding gap against $90.26bn of liquidity and a $25bn issuance already completed. The constraint is the rating agencies' patience - roughly $36bn of headroom, about three months of capex.
Meta's average ROIC is among the best in the listed world and has been for a decade: 36.85% in 2025 against an estimated 9.4% WACC. No serious bear case can ignore it.

Incremental ROIC on the 2025-28 capital vintage is 1.4-6.4% against a 9.5% WACC. The legacy franchise's excess returns are funding a programme that earns below its cost of capital - the exact failure mode the growth-is-not-value guardrail exists to detect.

The spread turns durably positive at a 35.3% FY2028 operating margin, versus 41.4% in 2025 and 33.7% estimated for 2026. Achievable, and the base case, but it requires the capex plateau rather than a demand surprise.

The dominant sensitivity is the discount rate, not the income statement. A 100bp WACC move is worth ~17% of equity value against ~$1bn a year to the credit; the 10-year at 4.79% is already the largest driver of the twelve-month de-rating.
thesisImpact: Explains Phase 3's margin failure and shows how much of it is reversible: the franchise earns 37% on capital while the new capital earns 1-6%. The repair condition is arithmetically specific - a 35.3% FY2028 operating margin - and sits within management's control. This converts the case from a quality judgement into a timing judgement on one variable, and it tells Phase 5 to weight down a DCF whose terminal value carries 87% of the answer.
